bullets.title: Big Tech AI capex hits investor patience: AMZN -7%, INTC -25% premarket on guidance misses
bullets.body: Amazon AWS grew 39% YoY (missing buyside 42-43% expectations) while capex surged to $77B vs $58B consensus, pushing TTM FCF to -$42B. Intel guided Q4 revenue to $15-16B, roughly $2B below the $17B Street estimate, on PC weakness and a $300M Fab 28 Israel explosion impact. Combined with RBLX, RDDT, and PINS guide cuts, Nasdaq futures are off ~250bps and S&P ~110bps.

bullets.title: AMZN AWS $578B backlog, 40%+ growth guided 2027-28; market focused on FCF burn
bullets.body: Despite missing Q3 AWS growth expectations, Amazon's backlog rose $82B QoQ to $578B and management guided AWS to exceed 40% growth in both 2027 and 2028, targeting a $1T annual revenue run rate in 5-10 years. JPM raised 2027 capex estimate to $395B and now expects negative FCF of -$128B in 2027, creating the key debate around whether AI monetization can catch up to infrastructure spending.

bullets.title: INTC PC collapse worsens: CY26 units -12%, CY27 -10%; foundry/server strength insufficient offset
bullets.body: Intel's client computing segment is expected to fall >20% QoQ in Q4 with PC units down ~12% in CY26 and a further ~10% TAM decline in CY27, driven by DRAM constraints and inventory correction persisting into 1H27. DCAI revenue grew 78% YoY and beat consensus, but supply constraints from the Israel fab incident and substrate shortages cap upside. Multiple analysts cut price targets (BofA to $100, MS to $75, Roth to $70) while maintaining a range of ratings.

bullets.title: AI capex sustainability questioned: 'self-reinforcing cycle' risk as core business growth slows
bullets.body: With hyperscalers (AMZN ~$220B, GOOGL ~$200B, MSFT ~$170B) guiding capex meaningfully higher into 2027 while core businesses show deceleration, market sentiment is shifting to scrutiny of AI ROI. Big Tech collectively lost nearly $900B in market cap on the session as FCF burn widened and non-AI segment growth disappointed. MSFT's $25B bond issuance — its first since 2017 — signals the shift to external financing to fund AI infrastructure.

bullets.title: Russell 2000 outperforms: +1.0% on day, +2.7% weekly vs S&P; small-cap breadth rotation underway
bullets.body: The Russell 2000 gained 1.0% on the day, outperforming the S&P 500 by 130bps, and is up 2.7% for the week vs S&P (+2.0% outperformance). YTD the index is up 15.2%, 240bps ahead of large caps. Discretionary, Industrials, and Financials led within the index; Tech, Staples, and Energy lagged. Equal-weight S&P is also outperforming as broadening rotation continues.

bullets.title: Macro factor call: long Cash Return, neutral broad AI basket, short Retail/Banks/Transports on hawkish inflation
bullets.body: With inflation trends remaining hawkish and AI names' EPS reactions failing to support broad AI outperformance, strategists recommend staying long the Cash Return factor (the one factor holding all year not driven by idiosyncratic risk) while going neutral on the broad AI basket into year-end. The Quality factor has lagged due to AI/Software idiosyncratic exposure. Market-wide calls are less reliable; narrower industry-level positioning is more rewarding.

bullets.title: Hedgeye signals: NASDAQ bearish trend, SPX bullish; rotate defensives XLV/XLP, short XLK/semis
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags NASDAQ Composite in bearish trend (25742-26593 range) while SPX remains bullish (7612-7779). The 10yr Treasury yield moved to Neutral TREND for the first time since July, key for the housing bull case. Hedgeye recommends rotating out of XLK and semis, going long XLV (+2.4% prior session) and XLP (+1.5%), and adding to short industrials (XLI). VIX in bullish trend at 16-21 range.

bullets.title: Short squeeze risk building for November: avg +1.9% seasonals, four catalysts identified
bullets.body: UBS flags that hyperscaler de-grossing has pushed short exposure above the 80th percentile (5-year) while retail investors bought the MSFT/GOOGL dip for the sixth time this month (RMM flow 72nd percentile vs. 3-year). With November averaging +1.9% since 1950 and four potential catalysts (midterm uncertainty subsiding, oil seasonality, volatility decline, yield pressure), a short squeeze setup is building in tech.

bullets.title: SNDK AI NAND demand structural: 50% FY27 bits under contract, datacenter to exceed 50% of demand in CY27
bullets.body: SanDisk beat Q1 revenue ($11.03B vs $10.72B guide) and EPS ($49.51 vs $46.67) on AI-driven storage demand, with datacenter now ~45-50% of revenue. The NBM pipeline covers 50% of FY27 bits and two-thirds of FY28 bits under long-term agreements, with commitments extending beyond FY30 and supply already sold out through end of decade. Datacenter bit demand expected to grow ~40% in CY27. SNDK also announced an 8-for-1 stock split effective Nov 19.

bullets.title: Google AI Mode disrupting search traffic, pressuring RDDT and ad ecosystem
bullets.body: Google's AI Mode is generating ~1M/week search referral loss for Reddit sustained into Q4, potentially driving low-double-digit DAU declines. RDDT's Q3 ad revenue grew 54% YoY on pricing and impressions, but 60% of DAUs are logged-out with minimal monetization. The broader implication for search-dependent digital media and advertising is negative, with GOOGL's own search revenue growth decelerating despite accelerating query volumes.

bullets.title: 3Q26 S&P 500 earnings: 77% beat rate, +4.6% above estimates; Big Tech lagging rest of market
bullets.body: With 57.7% of S&P 500 market cap reported, earnings are beating by 4.6% with a 77% upside surprise rate. Consensus expects 29.5% EPS growth for the quarter. The Big-6 TECH+ is expected at 21.8% EPS growth vs. 32.1% for the rest of the market, with Energy at 141.8% and Financials at 9.2% leading. Russell 2000 earnings are leading 5.6% above expectations (8.7% ex-financials).

bullets.title: Euro area 3Q26 GDP 0.8% annualized (ex-Ireland); France contracts, Spain outperforms at 2.6%
bullets.body: Euro area GDP printed 0.8% annualized ex-Ireland (1.7% including Ireland volatility), below the 1.0% forecast. Germany came in at 0.9%, while France contracted -0.5%. Italian headline inflation surged to 5.6% on regulated energy prices. The 4Q26 forecast is maintained at 1.5% but carries downside risks from continued energy pressure and French political unrest.

bullets.title: Europe 2027 political risk: half the euro area voting; structural fiscal deficits widening by 3pp of GDP by 2040
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flags major 2027 elections in France (presidential April/May + possible snap elections June), Italy, Spain, and Greece as political uncertainty mounts alongside rising bond yields. Europe's fiscal challenge is structural — ageing, defence, and interest costs will mechanically widen deficits by at least 3pp of GDP by 2040 in most euro area countries. Greece remains the standout with EM-to-DM equity upgrade still only halfway played out.

bullets.title: Crypto shock: Binance $6.3B security breach weighs on sentiment; Coinbase positioned as share-gainer
bullets.body: A compromised device triggered $6.3B in unauthorized withdrawals from Binance, with ~$3B frozen on-chain via Tether ($1.57B), Circle ($800M+), and Ripple ($200M). Binance said user funds are safe and losses covered by SAFU. KeyBanc expects near-term trading activity headwinds across crypto but sees Coinbase as a share-gain opportunity, with fair value at $155 on 17.8x CY27 EV/EBITDA.

bullets.title: Oil +1.3-1.8% as Iran tensions escalate; WTI at $104.16
bullets.body: WTI crude rose 1.3% to $104.16 and Brent gained 1.8% as Iran's Parliament Speaker demanded U.S. acceptance of seven conditions for negotiations, and reports of possible U.S. military action surfaced. Oil is in Hedgeye's bullish TREND regime. The commodity move is also feeding into margin headwinds for transportation-heavy sectors.

bullets.title: Agricultural price premium erosion overstates supply comfort; China $17B purchase commitment unfulfilled
bullets.body: The BCOM Agri Index has retreated from a 24% YTD peak to ~8.5% as risk premiums eroded, but JPM argues fundamentals do not justify this — global stocks-to-use ratios are tightening into 2027/28 amid weather-related yield declines and firm biofuel demand. China has yet to meaningfully commence its $17B annual purchase commitment for U.S. ag products ex-soybeans, representing underpriced upside risk in CBOT Corn, Wheat, and ICE Cotton.

bullets.title: PC supply chain read-throughs: DELL/HPE at risk; AAPL and premium commercial better positioned
bullets.body: Intel's guidance implies CY27 PC unit TAM down 10% with pronounced 1H declines from memory-driven pricing increases, a negative read-through for HPE and HP. Citi and Morgan Stanley both flag Apple and Dell as better positioned given exposure to premium consumers, commercial markets, and AI-driven server/storage demand. Server CPU units, conversely, are expected to grow >30% in both CY26 and CY27.

bullets.title: US restaurant traffic decelerating: industry footfall -2.1% YoY for week ending 10/25
bullets.body: Citi's weekly tracker shows restaurant industry footfall contracted 2.1% YoY (worse than -1.9% prior week). LSR fell -2.8% with McDonald's -5.4% and Wendy's -11.2%, while Burger King was a standout at +8.9%. Fast casual grew 1.5% but decelerated 190bps WoW. BEA September data shows restaurant spending annualized +10.4% MoM and FAFH gained 17bps share vs. FAH in real terms.

bullets.title: Floor & Decor cuts FY26 guidance; October comps -3.8% signal consumer home improvement demand slump
bullets.body: FND lowered FY26 EPS guidance to $1.88-$1.98 (from $1.88-$2.13), revenue to $4.765-4.835B, and EBITDA to $535-550M while halving store openings to 10-15 from 20 for 2027. October comps decelerated to -3.8% from Q3's -1.4%. Macro headwinds cited include mortgage rates, existing home sales, fuel costs, and consumer sentiment — a cautionary signal for housing-linked consumer spending.

bullets.title: Key earnings next week: AAPL Mon, AMD/ANET/BKNG Tue, SNAP/HUBS/EXPE Wed
bullets.body: AAPL reports Monday Nov 2 after close (EPS $1.99 expected, revenue $113.4B). AMD reports Tuesday Nov 3 (EPS $1.95, revenue $13.09B). ANET reports Tuesday (EPS $1.08, revenue $3.33B). SNAP, HUBS, and EXPE all report Wednesday Nov 4. Buyside sentiment on AAPL is -2/5 (bearish) and AMD is +3/5 (bullish) per JPM chip checks.
